builder_plan.scenario: A multi-step product task fails because the agent loses track of dependencies.
builder_plan.change: Try the proposed planning step on tasks with checkable intermediate outcomes.
builder_plan.baseline: The same agent solving the same tasks without the new planning step.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task completion, unnecessary steps, planning tokens, response time, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Combining Hierarchical Cognitive Process with Process Supervision for Interpretable Scene Safety Understanding
summary: The method replaces direct scene-to-safety-level mapping models with an LLM-based framework that follows a hierarchical cognitive structure, using process-labeled multi-step reasoning data and LoRA with Mixture-of-Experts expert modules specialized per reasoning sub-process. It costs a new process-labeled dataset (which the authors construct), fine-tuning infrastructure for LLM plus MoE adapter training that likely exceeds a single 24 GB GPU for larger base models, and added orchestration complexity across expert modules. It can fail through error propagation between hierarchical reasoning steps, dependence on the quality and domain coverage of the process-labeled dataset, and interpretability gains that do not guarantee correct safety judgments in out-of-distribution scenes.
rationale: The approach targets a niche safety-critical benchmark and requires dataset construction plus LLM fine-tuning with MoE specialization, with no quantified gains reported, so it warrants monitoring rather than adoption under constrained infrastructure.
technique: Hierarchical process-supervised safety reasoning with LoRA-MoE
